sections.h2: What an Iowa quitclaim deed transfers
sections.html:
A quitclaim deed hands over whatever interest the signer holds, and promises nothing beyond that. Iowa Code 558.19 gives a sample quitclaim form: it names a consideration in dollars and says the grantor quitclaims to the grantee all interest in a described tract.

The same statute has sample forms for a fee simple deed without warranty, which uses the words "hereby convey," and for a warranty deed, which adds a warranty of title against all persons. Each form is sufficient if varied to suit the circumstances, so the quitclaim is a valid way to move title. What changes is the promise the grantor makes.

For that reason a quitclaim suits transfers between people who already know the property's history, such as adding a spouse or placing a house into a family arrangement. It is a poor fit when a stranger is paying money and wants a promise about title.

sections.h2: Recording costs at the county recorder
sections.html:
Recording usually runs $5 per page plus two $1 charges, and transfer tax can be added if money changed hands. The recorder's schedule comes from Iowa Code 331.604.

ChargeAmount
Recording a real estate instrument$5 per page or fraction, per transaction
Records management fund$1 per recorded transaction
Electronic transaction fund$1 per recorded transaction
Transfer tax80 cents per $500 or fraction over the first $500 of consideration
Groundwater hazard statementNo recorder fee

Some counties add services or rules of their own, so phone the recorder before you mail a deed.

sections.h2: How should the deed be formatted for the recorder?
sections.html:
Each recorder sets its own format rules. The Story County Recorder publishes a clear list, which makes a handy model. Its deeds need:

  • At least three inches of blank space at the top of the first page.
  • The preparer's name, address and phone number typed directly below that space.
  • The line "Address Tax Statement To" with the taxpayer's name and address, right under the preparer information.
  • A full legal description, never the shortened one printed on a tax statement.
  • Printed names beneath every signature, including the acknowledging officer.
  • A signed, dated and notarized document that is legible and reproducible.

Other counties vary in small ways. The Story County recording requirements page has the full list.

sections.h2: Notarizing the deed, including remote notarization
sections.html:
A deed has to be acknowledged before a notarial officer to be lawfully recorded (558.42), and the acknowledgment follows Chapter 9B (558.20). The signer declares that the signature is theirs and was given for the stated purpose. An entity signer must have authority.

The officer confirms identity through personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence. Good evidence includes a passport, driver's license or government nondriver ID that is current or expired no more than three years, or a credible witness. The officer can refuse to proceed if unsure that the signer has capacity or is signing knowingly and voluntarily.

Remote notarization is allowed under 9B.14A. Notary and signer must communicate by sight and sound. Identity needs personal knowledge, a credible witness or two types of identity proofing. The notary makes an audio-visual recording and keeps it for at least ten years, and the certificate must say technology was used. Ask the recorder whether the county will accept the resulting document.

sections.h2: When a quitclaim deed owes Iowa transfer tax
sections.html:
Transfer tax applies only when consideration is above $500. The rate is 80 cents for each $500 or fraction over $500, and the person conveying the property owes it (428A.1 and 428A.3).

Many family and court-driven transfers are exempt under 428A.2. The exemptions most likely to touch a quitclaim are:

  • Deeds between spouses, or between parent and child, without actual consideration. Cancelling debt secured by the property is not actual consideration if it stays within the property's fair market value.
  • Deeds between former spouses under a dissolution decree.
  • Deeds that correct, confirm or supplement a recorded deed with no added consideration.
  • Deeds returning property to lienholders in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Deeds distributing trust assets to beneficiaries without consideration.

A recorder will not accept an exempt deed without a signed statement claiming the exemption, filed with the deed or endorsed on it (428A.4). Knowingly skipping tax that is due, or willfully entering false information on a declaration of value, is a simple misdemeanor (428A.10 and 428A.15).

sections.h2: Declaration of value and groundwater hazard statement
sections.html:
Both forms travel with the deed. The declaration of value reports the full consideration. At least one seller or buyer, or an agent, must sign it, and it is required unless the deed falls in an exempt category. The recorder does not record it; the data goes to the assessor (428A.1).

The groundwater hazard statement under 558.69 covers known burial sites, wells, solid waste disposal sites, underground storage tanks, hazardous waste and private sewage systems. The owner is responsible for getting it right. If none of those conditions exist, the first page of the deed carries the exemption statement. A recorder must refuse a deed missing the required statement, though a deed recorded without it is not void.

The groundwater process has worked differently since July 1, 2022 (House File 2343), so use the current form from the recorder.

sections.h2: Does a spouse have to sign?
sections.html:
Often yes. When the owner is married, conveying the homestead is not valid unless the other spouse signs the same or a like instrument, or a power of attorney for it (561.13).

A spouse who holds only homestead rights and a statutory share can relinquish those rights specifically under 597.5 without joining the granting clause. The signature requirement does not apply if a dissolution decree ended the interest, if the right of recovery is barred under 614.15, for a purchase-money mortgage, or where a court of equity finds that undoing the transaction would unjustly enrich the other spouse.

The homestead is the owner's home plus the contiguous land used with it. Inside a city plat it is capped at one half acre, and outside a plat at forty acres (561.1 and 561.2).

sections.h2: When a quitclaim is the wrong tool for selling
sections.html:
An unrecorded instrument is invalid against later good-faith purchasers for value without notice, so recording promptly protects the new owner (558.41). Quitclaim transfers are also excluded from the seller disclosure requirement, one reason families use them between relatives.

Other recording rules depend on the property. Entity transfers carry implied warranties unless the deed says otherwise, including that the entity exists and the signer is authorized (558.72). A grantee of agricultural land must record within 180 days (558.44).

If you plan to sell, ask the buyer or title company which form they want before you sign anything. A buyer paying cash will usually expect a warranty or a title policy behind the deed. Owners with liens, back taxes or unclear co-owners should get advice first, since a quitclaim does not clear any of those problems; it only passes along what the signer owns.

A practical order of steps: pull the current deed, confirm every owner on it, get payoff figures for any loans, then decide on the form. Bring the deed, photo ID for each signer and the legal description to the notary appointment, and have the declaration of value filled out before the recorder sees the packet.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed legal in Iowa?
faqs.a: Yes. Iowa Code 558.19 lists the quitclaim form beside fee simple deeds without warranty and with warranty as sufficient ways to convey.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record an Iowa quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Recording is $5 per page or fraction, plus $1 for the records management fund and $1 for the electronic transaction fund per recorded transaction. Transfer tax applies only if consideration exceeds $500.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need to be notarized in Iowa?
faqs.a: Yes. A deed must be acknowledged under Chapter 9B before it can be lawfully recorded. Remote notarization is allowed when the statutory conditions are met.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed remove my spouse's homestead rights?
faqs.a: Not by itself. A married owner's homestead conveyance is invalid without the spouse's signature on the same or a like instrument, with limited exceptions.

faqs.q: Can I quitclaim my house to my child without paying transfer tax in Iowa?
faqs.a: A deed between parent and child without actual consideration is exempt under 428A.2. You must claim the exemption in a signed statement, and recording fees still apply.
